notes.text: Brandon Hagel is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
Zemgus Girgensons is on injured reserve (upper body injury) and missed their last game. Anthony Cirelli has taken his spot beside Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev.
Sam O'Reilly was added to the roster on Nov 12 and has played beside Yanni Gourde and Gage Goncalves.
John Carlson is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 22 games, down from 47% with his old team last season.

faceoff.text: Anthony Cirelli is sent out to take power-play faceoffs, then changes. He has taken 29% of the team’s power-play draws but stays on for about 40 seconds at a time, against 78 for the regulars, and is most often replaced by Brandon Hagel (6 of 10 changes).

stakes: The Hurricanes go in first in the Metropolitan with 35 points, the Lightning tied for first in the Atlantic with 32 points.

TBL.head: Close, but the Hurricanes have the slight edge
TBL.body: Even though Tampa Bay has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Tampa Bay will be without Hagel. The Lightning can tip it if they get good looks.

CAR.head: The Hurricanes start a half-step ahead
CAR.body: Even though Tampa Bay has home-ice advantage, Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately. On top of that, Tampa Bay will be without Hagel. Still, it’s close: the Lightning can make it interesting if they get good looks.

story.head: Clash of the titans
paras: The Lightning have won two in a row, while the Hurricanes (16-3-3) lost 2-1 in overtime to Montréal on Thursday. Two of the league’s best teams meet. Going in, the Hurricanes are first in the Metropolitan (third in the NHL) and the Bolts first in the Atlantic (tied for fourth).

The Hurricanes take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st). They also give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd), so the Lightning could find some good looks against them. Carolina has scored 4.00 goals a game, the most in the league, and allowed 2.18, the second fewest. The Lightning ice the puck less than almost anyone (2nd) and draw more penalties than they take (4th). They also keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd), and something has to give when the Hurricanes’ shooting runs into their defense. Tampa Bay has scored 3.73 goals a game, the fourth most in the league.

Sebastian Aho (12 G / 17 A / 29 P in 22 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for tenth in the NHL, with eight points in his last five games. Andrei Svechnikov (11 G / 10 A / 21 P in 22 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. Nikita Kucherov (9 G / 22 A / 31 P in 22 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring and is eighth in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games and six goals in eight games against Carolina since 2023-24. Jake Guentzel (13 G / 14 A / 27 P in 22 GP) has a team-high 13 goals, tied for seventh in the NHL, with nine points in his last five games.
Pyotr Kochetkov (12-1-1 / .920 SV% in 14 GS) has been terrific for Carolina and will likely start. Andrei Vasilevskiy (11-5-1 / .895 SV% in 17 GS) is in line to start for Tampa Bay.
At home, Jon Cooper likes to send Gourde, O'Reilly and Goncalves out against opponents’ third lines, so watch for them against Martinook, Staal and Jarvis.
